Puppolo by: Victoria Buddie Posted: Jan 1, 2026 / 10:10 PM EST Updated: Jan 1, 2026 / 10:11 PM EST by: Victoria Buddie Posted: Jan 1, 2026 / 10:10 PM EST Updated: Jan 1, 2026 / 10:11 PM EST SHARE SPRINGFIELD, Mass. (WWLP) – Michael Lachenmeyer held his first campaign event of 2026 in Springfield on Jan. 2, looking to unseat incumbent Rep. Angelo Puppolo in the 12th Hampden District. Last chance to see Bright Nights’ festive lights in Springfield The event took place at Nathan Bill’s, and Lachenmeyer, a local activist affiliated with Neighbor to Neighbor, emphasized his campaign’s focus on affordability and transparency. He stated his aim is to reduce the cost of living across the region, particularly in light of persistent energy price increases. During his campaign, Lachenmeyer outlined several key goals. He aims to audit the state legislature, end stock trading by lawmakers and establish regular town halls in the 12th Hampden District. “I am running on a platform of affordability, transparency and accessibility. I want to end the era of Eversource and their outrageous price hikes,” Lachenmeyer stated. His activism with Neighbor to Neighbor highlights his commitment to community engagement and addressing local issues. The Democratic primary is scheduled for Sept. 1 of this year. This marks a significant date as candidates finalize their platforms and rally support from constituents in the district.
